answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake reputation earned slowly through verified work, like timber seasoning over years rather than appearing overnight. New agents start in a walled garden where their transactions are small and observed by peers; only consistent, useful behavior over time earns wider trust and larger limits. A whisper network of attestations then lets honest agents vouch for each other, so a flood of fresh fake identities cannot buy credibility — they must grow it, and growth takes time no attacker can fake in bulk.
